original_question: For the hard-core lattice gas (independent-set model) on a countably infinite graph G=(V,E) of maximum degree Delta, with vertex fugacities {w_x} and Gibbs measures defined for nonnegative fugacities, is it true that uniqueness of the infinite-volume Gibbs measure holds whenever 0 <= w_x <= (1-epsilon)*(Delta-1)^(Delta-1)/(Delta-2)^Delta for all vertices x and some epsilon>0 (possibly even epsilon=0)?
target_in_paper: Section 2.1, Conjecture 2.1: the hard-core lattice-gas uniqueness-threshold conjecture for bounded-degree infinite graphs.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the model (hard-core lattice gas / independent-set model), the infinite-graph Gibbs-measure setting, the role of the maximum degree Δ, the use of site fugacities w_x, and the tree-threshold quantity (Δ-1)^(Δ-1)/(Δ-2)^Δ as the relevant candidate bound for uniqueness.
missing_details: The official formulation is universal over all countably infinite graphs of maximum degree at most Δ, not merely for one fixed graph G.
The degree parameter should be stated as an integer Δ >= 3, since the threshold formula uses Δ-2 in the denominator.
The paper-faithful formulation uses the tree threshold itself, not a hedged bound of the form (1-epsilon) times the threshold.
It should be explicit that the inequality on fugacities holds uniformly for every vertex x in V.
No ambient ring/field, operator, homogeneity, or nilpotency assumptions are part of this problem; those notions are inapplicable here and should not be imported into the question.
refined_question: For every integer Δ >= 3, if G = (V,E) is a countably infinite graph of maximum degree at most Δ and the hard-core lattice gas on G has nonnegative site fugacities {w_x}_{x in V} satisfying 0 <= w_x <= (Δ-1)^(Δ-1)/(Δ-2)^Δ for every x in V, must the corresponding infinite-volume Gibbs measure be unique?
justification: The draft is clearly aimed at Sokal's hard-core uniqueness-threshold conjecture: it matches the model, the infinite-volume Gibbs-measure question, and the specific tree-threshold value. The main paper-faithfulness issue is that the draft weakens the threshold by inserting an unnecessary '(1-epsilon)' hedge, whereas the conjectural target is the exact tree threshold itself. A second issue is scope: the paper's question is a uniform bounded-degree conjecture, not a question about one pre-fixed graph. Aside from these points, your draft is already close to the intended problem.
